problem:
Express $\frac{4-5x}{x(x-1)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.

| $\frac{4-5x}{x(x-1)}=\,$ | {{field-1}} | $+$ | {{field-2}} |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $x$ |  | $x-1$ |
worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\frac{4-5x}{x(x-1)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x-1}.
$$

Multiplying both sides by $x(x-1)$ gives

$$
4-5x=A(x-1)+Bx.
$$

For $x=0$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4-5(0) & =A(0-1)+B(0) \\ 4 & =-A \\ A & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=1,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4-5(1) & =A(1-1)+B(1) \\ -1 & =B \\ B & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{4-5x}{x(x-1)}=\frac{-4}{x}+\frac{-1}{x-1}.
$$
